description: We are a passionate team of student developers interested in AI, Machine Learning, software development and innovation. Our project, FieldShift AI, uses NASA satellite data and machine learning to help farmers understand climate changes, predict agricultural risks and make smarter crop decisions. We believe in teamwork, creativity and building technology that solves real-world problems. Our goal is to promote sustainable agriculture through intelligent, accessible and data-driven solutions.
summary: Field Shift is a full-stack agricultural decision-support web application built for NASA Space Apps 2026 that helps farmers transition away from repetitive monoculture farming toward climate-resilient, sustainable 2-crop rotations.   By dropping a pin on an interactive map, users trigger real-time queries to the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API to retrieve localized precipitation, extreme temperatures, root-zone soil wetness, and solar irradiance. The Python FastAPI backend evaluates 18 global crops using a SMART Multi-Criteria Decision Algorithm combined with peer-reviewed agronomic rules—rewarding botanical family breaks, alternating deep and shallow roots, prioritizing drought-tolerant crops when soil wetness drops below $0.45$, and adjusting legume nitrogen bonuses under extreme heat ($>35^\circ\text{C}$).   Field Shift outputs the top three ranked crop rotations alongside Sustainable Yield Index ($SYI$), Crop Production Resilience ($R_c$), and Water Savings Percentage metrics compared against a monoculture baseline. Built with React, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Recharts, FastAPI, and Supabase, the platform logs farm analyses and delivers actionable, climate-adapted planting guidance.
details:
Project Details: Field ShiftWhat It Does & How It Works

Field Shift is a full-stack agricultural decision-support web application built for NASA Space Apps 2026 that helps farmers transition away from repetitive monoculture farming toward climate-resilient, sustainable 2-crop rotations. Hyper-Local NASA Telemetry: Users drop a pin anywhere on an interactive map (or choose from global climate presets) and set their current crop and priorities (Water Conservation, Soil Health, Yield Stability, and Low Input Cost). The backend queries the zero-authentication NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (community=AG) to fetch precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), maximum/minimum temperatures (T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT), and surface solar irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), generating automatic climate risk alerts. Explainable Agronomic Scoring Engine: Using a SMART Multi-Criteria Decision Algorithm (0–100 scale) paired with peer-reviewed agronomic rules, Field Shift evaluates 18 global crops against a monoculture baseline ([Current Crop, Current Crop]). It outputs the top 3 ranked crop rotations alongside Sustainable Yield Index ($SYI$), Crop Production Resilience ($R_c$), Water Savings Percentage, and localized risk advisories. Benefits & Intended ImpactClimate Adaptation & Yield Stability: Moving from continuous monoculture to a scientifically paired 2-crop rotation increases resilience by up to 3.7× compared to adding a third crop, reduces annual evapotranspiration, and offsets climate-induced cereal yield losses. Resource & Soil Preservation: Alternating botanical families and deep/shallow root architectures disrupts pest cycles, improves soil aggregate stability (by up to 35%), and reduces irrigation water demand. Actionable Accessibility: Translates raw NASA Earth observation parameters into plain-language planting sequences and risk callouts that smallholder farmers and local extension officers can act on immediately.Tools, Languages & Software StackFrontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, react-leaflet (interactive geospatial pin-drop map), Recharts (grouped comparative bar charts), and Lucide React—deployed on Netlify ([https://hexa-coders.netlify.app](https://hexa-coders.netlify.app)). Backend & Science Engine: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, and requests (with lru_cache coordinate caching)—deployed on Render ([https://field-shift-e73n.onrender.com](https://field-shift-e73n.onrender.com)).Database & Data Sources: NASA POWER Agroclimatology REST API (satellite climate telemetry) and Supabase (PostgreSQL) for logging farm rotation analyses (
